text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on December 11 in history.
1475 - Pope Leo X born as Giovanni de Medici; he was an extravagant pontiff who helped make Rome a centre of European culture.
1803 - Hector Berlioz, French composer of "Symphonie Fantastique" and "Romeo et Juliette", born.
1816 - Indiana became the 19th state of the United States.
1843 - German physician and bacteriologist Robert Koch born; noted for his discovery of the anthrax, tubercle and cholera bacilli.
1845 - A defence union was set up by the Catholic Swiss cantons to oppose anti-Catholic measures by Protestant cantons. The union, and the civil war that followed, became known as the Sonderbund.
1856 - Georgy Plekhanov, leading Marxist theorist in Russia, born.
1882 - Fiorello La Guardia, colourful three-term mayor of New York City, born.
1886 - Victor McLaglen, film actor and Oscar winner for "The Informer", born. He was also well-known for his roles in "The Quiet Man" and "She Wore a Yellow Ribbon".
1894 - The world's first motor show opened in Paris with nine exhibitors.
1899 - At the battle of Magersfontein in the second British-Boer war, a British advance was thwarted with the loss of over 1,000 men.
1913 - Italian film director Carlo Ponti born; husband of Sophia Loren, he was best known for "Dr. Zhivago" and "The Cassandra Crossing".
1917 - Sir Mackenzie Bowell, Canadian statesman and Prime Minister, died.
1918 - Alexander Solzhenitsyn born. The most notable literary talent in Russia since the revolution, he was exiled in 1974 for refusing to keep silent about his country's past.
1930 - The Bank of the United States in New York failed in another indication of the Great Depression.
1936 - Edward VIII's abdication as King of Great Britain became effective; he gave up the throne in order to marry American divorcee Wallis Simpson.
1937 - The Fascist Council in Rome withdrew Italy from the League of Nations.
1941 - Italy and Germany declared war on the United States; the U.S. Congress in turn declared war on both.
1946 - The United Nations International Children's Emergency Fund (UNICEF) was created by the U.N. General Assembly to provide relief to children in countries devasted by war.
1967 - The prototype of the Anglo-French supersonic aircraft Concorde was shown for the first time at Toulouse, France.

1973 - West German Chancellor Willy Brandt and Czech Prime Minister Lubomir Strougal formally signed a treaty nullifying the 1938 Munich pact which sanctioned Hitler's seizure of Czechoslovakia's Sudetenland.
1983 - After widespread riots, Bangladesh's Chief Martial Law Administrator, Mohammad Ershad, declared himself president.
1990 - Albania's ruling Communist Party authorised the establishment of opposition political parties.
1992 - In what was hoped would be an end to civil war in Somalia, warlords Ali Mahdi Mohamed and Mohamed Farah Aideed signed a peace plan.
1993 - After 45 years of talks, a United Nations panel approved the creation of a new Commissioner for Human Rights to respond quickly to major rights crises around the world.
1994 - Russia sent tanks and troops pouring into Chechnya to end the rebel territory's three-year unilateral drive for independence.
1995 - France replaced its U.N. commander in Sarajevo, Rene Bachelet, for criticising the Dayton peace deal.
